Definition: Bilam, a Mesopotamian prophet; also a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Balaam means not of the people, and he is the prophet hired to curse Israel who could only bless them. In Numbers 22:5 Balak sends for Balaam the son of Beor, and in Numbers 22:12 God tells him not to go, for the people are blessed. In Numbers 24:10 Balak's anger is kindled because Balaam has blessed them three times — and Joshua 13:22 ends the story plainly: Balaam the soothsayer did the children of Israel slay with the sword.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Balaam is the proof that no curse can stick where God has blessed, and the warning that a man can speak God's words and still love the wages of unrighteousness.
